requirements.title: Intrinsic operators comprise nine syntactic categories
requirements.definition: The intrinsic-operator syntactic class is the union of power-op, mult-op, add-op, concat-op, rel-op, not-op, and-op, or-op, and equiv-op. The member spellings are defined by the corresponding Clause 10 rules, which are restated here for reference. This union does not by itself specify operand types, numbers of operands, evaluation, or precedence, nor does membership require that every use be an intrinsic rather than a defined operation.
requirements.oracle: Nine separately compiled positive-control programs admit all nine categories in conforming intrinsic expressions. Together they use all 23 intrinsic spellings, including unary and binary add-op contexts. Integer computations, same-kind character concatenation, integer relations, and logical operations have direct literal result assertions. Each expression under test is assigned to a result before checking it; the expected result is not another invocation of the tested expression.
requirements.oracle_limitation: These are finite syntax/admission controls with runtime self-checks, not independent coverage of the Clause 10 token definitions, precedence, evaluation order, all operand type/kind/rank combinations, or generic dispatch. No R608-only malformed-token negative is manufactured: malformed member spellings belong to their canonical rules, and the one well-formed nonoperator exclusion in an actual OPERATOR generic context is assigned only to R609. The absence of a separate invalid file is a testing boundary, not an uncovered acceptance facet.
requirements.dependencies: 4.1.1 explains alternatives and later-clause restatements; 4.1.2 p2 makes associated constraints apply at every occurrence; 4.2 p2(3) requires diagnostic capability for syntax violations, not a particular severity or mandatory rejection. Canonical spellings: 10.1.2.5/R1008-R1010, 10.1.2.6/R1012, 10.1.2.7/R1014, and 10.1.2.8/R1019-R1022 (PDF pp169-171). 10.1.5, including Table 10.2, supplies the valid intrinsic operand/result premises and the assertion values. R610 and 10.1.6 distinguish extension uses.

requirements.title: Defined-operator admits named unary, named binary, and intrinsic extension forms
requirements.source: 6.2.4 R609; J3/24-007 PDF p70, printed p56, lines 6-8.
requirements.definition: A defined-operator is a defined-unary-op, a defined-binary-op, or an extended-intrinsic-op. The first two syntactic classes inherit their canonical Clause 10 definitions and constraints, and the third is supplied by R610. These alternatives can occupy the defined-operator position of an OPERATOR generic specification. A well-formed token outside all three classes, such as the assignment symbol, cannot occupy that position. The union does not itself define a procedure interface or make a particular operation applicable.
requirements.oracle: Use valid explicit interfaces for a named unary function, a named binary function, and unary and binary intrinsic extensions on derived-type operands. Independent literal checks establish that each conforming control executes meaningfully. Isolate one negative with INTERFACE OPERATOR (=): the assignment symbol is a well-formed Fortran token but not an R609 alternative. Its function has two nonoptional INTENT(IN) derived-type dummy arguments and an integer result. The minimally repaired control replaces only that operator-position token by +; both bodies call the helper by its specific name, so the negative has no additional bad expression or unresolved operator reference.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Do not attribute malformed dotted names, excessive operator-name length, reserved intrinsic/logical spellings, missing interfaces, wrong arity, or forbidden intrinsic signatures to this union. Those belong to R1004/C1005, R1024/C1006, or Clause 15. The one negative tests membership in a context that explicitly requires defined-operator, not every forbidden token. 4.2 requires diagnostic capability; the runner additionally expects rejection and a source-located error. A compiler accepting with a relevant diagnostic is not the same observation as silent acceptance.
requirements.dependencies: R1004/C1005 in 10.1.2.4 (PDF p169), R1024/C1006 in 10.1.2.9 (PDF p171), and local R610. R1503/R1506/R1508 and C1504/C1507/C1508 in 15.4.3.2 (PDF pp326-327) supply the generic-interface context and explicit procedure interfaces. 15.4.3.4.2 p1 (PDF p329) supplies nonoptional data dummies, INTENT(IN) or VALUE, one/two arguments, non-assumed-length results, and signatures distinct from intrinsic operations. 10.1.6.1-2 (PDF pp181-182) supplies applicability and function-defined interpretations; no type-bound or generic-resolution coverage is inferred. 4.2 p2(3) supplies the diagnostic-capability obligation.

requirements.title: An intrinsic extension retains an intrinsic operator spelling
requirements.source: 6.2.4 R610; J3/24-007 PDF p70, printed p56, line 11.
requirements.definition: The extended-intrinsic-op syntactic class is an alias for intrinsic-operator. It introduces no additional operator spelling. In the R609 alternative this permits an intrinsic operator token to identify a defined operation, provided the separate expression and procedure-interface requirements are met. It neither authorizes replacing an existing intrinsic signature nor establishes which function is selected.
requirements.oracle: Ten positive-control programs use explicit OPERATOR interfaces for all nine inherited categories. Unary and binary add-op extensions are separate programs; not-op is unary and the other sampled operations are binary. Every extension uses declared scalar derived-type operands, matching nonoptional INTENT(IN) dummies, and an explicit non-assumed-length result. Their signatures differ from all intrinsic signatures. Literal integer, character, or logical checks test the results of the chosen functions; the relational extension samples < rather than duplicating every relational spelling.
requirements.oracle_limitation: This alias has no independent rejection boundary once R608 and its member grammar are fixed, so no R610_invalid file is forced. Wrong extension arity, an intrinsic-signature collision, type-bound binding restrictions, generic ambiguity, and operand association defects are owned by Clause 15/10, not this alias. The controls do not claim all extension signatures, every relational synonym, mixed types, ranks, kinds, precedence, or dispatch semantics. They do not require a processor-dependent kind, floating-point tolerance, collating sequence, or optional feature.
requirements.dependencies: R608 supplies the nine categories and its Clause 10 references supply their spellings. 5.5.6 (PDF p66) distinguishes intrinsic and additional operators. 10.1.5.1/Table 10.2 (PDF p175), 10.1.6.1-2 (PDF pp181-182), and 15.4.3.4.2 p1-p3 (PDF p329) provide the valid intrinsic/defined-operation premises, intrinsic-compatible arity, distinct signatures, and interpretations. 15.4.3.2 supplies the explicit generic interfaces. These dependencies are not locally reauthored requirements. Syntax diagnostics inherit 4.2 p2(3); the alias is not an additional diagnostic policy.

review_rationale: Independent source-first review verified all three base units and 23 subdivisions, canonical ownership of the eleven Clause 10 restatements, category-admission limits, conforming defined/extended operator interfaces, and the one-token OPERATOR(=) to OPERATOR(+) repair. Detailed precedence, operand matrices, and assignment semantics are not claimed.
